excerpt_text: I first noticed warmth across my chest. The situation had not changed, but my attention was no longer trapped by the worry.
interpretive_memo: Body sensation and attentional movement are narrated together.

excerpt_text: The tears came before I could explain anything. I understood them as relief and as being known by God.
interpretive_memo: Tears acquire meaning through a perceived relationship.

excerpt_text: During prayer I felt loved rather than judged. That changed the story I had been telling about myself.
interpretive_memo: Divine relationship supports a revised self-narrative.

excerpt_text: The peace was intense that evening, but what made it last was talking about it with people who knew me well.
interpretive_memo: Community is described as a mechanism of durability.

excerpt_text: I was grateful the next morning, although the old fear returned later. Recovery felt more like a rhythm than a single cure.
interpretive_memo: The account resists a simple permanent-transformation story.

excerpt_text: I could choose whether to continue the prayer and I remained able to work. That sense of control mattered to how I understood it.
interpretive_memo: Agency and functioning help describe, not diagnose, the experience.

excerpt_text: A scripture phrase became personally vivid. It did not sound audible, but it felt addressed to my exact situation.
interpretive_memo: The participant carefully distinguishes vividness from external sound.

excerpt_text: At first I kept the experience private because I was unsure what others would call it. The small group gave me language for it.
interpretive_memo: Shared language organizes an initially ambiguous event.

excerpt_text: I still had difficult days, but the memory of being accompanied changed how alone the difficulty felt.
interpretive_memo: Persistence lies in a changed relation to distress, not its disappearance.

excerpt_text: The experience became frightening when I could not sleep and felt pushed to act. I sought help from both a clinician and my pastor.
interpretive_memo: The synthetic case demonstrates a dual clinical and community response.

excerpt_text: Singing with other people made the presence feel stronger than when I prayed alone, though the quiet prayer felt more intimate.
interpretive_memo: Different practices shape distinct qualities rather than a single intensity scale.

excerpt_text: Weeks later I could not reproduce the same warmth. What remained was a more patient way of responding to fear.
interpretive_memo: A transient sensation is distinguished from longer behavioral integration.
